dedupe_keys.name: bicycles and micromobility for disaster response and recovery expert workshop synthesis

description: This open-access paper synthesises what is known about using bicycles and other micromobility in disaster response and recovery. Dillon Fitch, Chen Chen and Stephen Wong published it in Transport Policy in 2024 after convening an online workshop with disaster experts from government agencies, non-profit organisations, academia and policy groups, combining brainstorming and focus group discussion with a literature review. Bicycles have been used anecdotally in past disasters to save lives and help communities recover, but research and practice are scarce. The authors find strong potential across disaster phases, hazard types and population groups, and identify barriers of implementation and safety that call for research and policy in both transport and emergency management. Coverage: general, drawing on international experience. Access: open-access article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: qualitative expert views and a review, with no quantitative dataset or model; conclusions are indicative. It can inform emergency response and resilience scenarios that add active modes to evacuation and recovery models. It relates to bike share data such as Citi Bike and to the PeopleForBikes network analysis in the catalogue.
